“Mañjuśrī! If there are sentient beings who can be transformed, and who should see the color of the King of Wish-Fulfilling Jewels called ‘The Sound of the Great Ocean of Entering the Three Times Emerging from Incalculable Eons,’ then the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, immediately manifest it for them, enabling those sentient beings to behold the color of the Tathāgata—the King of Wish-Fulfilling Jewels called ‘The Sound of the Great Ocean of Entering the Three Times Emerging from Incalculable Eons’—without any obstruction.”

“Mañjuśrī! If there are sentient beings who can be transformed, and who should see the color of the Wish-Fulfilling Jewel King named ‘The Sound of the Great Ocean of the Mind of Unwearied Entry into the Inconceivable (*asaṃkhyeya*)’—then the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, immediately manifest it for them, enabling those sentient beings to behold the color of the Tathāgata’s ‘Wish-Fulfilling Jewel King named The Sound of the Great Ocean of the Mind of Unwearied Entry into the Inconceivable’ without any hindrance.”

“Mañjuśrī! If there are sentient beings who can be transformed, and who should see the color of the King of Wish-Fulfilling Jewels named ‘The Sound of the Ocean of Non-differentiated Wisdom that Causes Entry into the Inconceivable,’ then the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, immediately manifest it for them. Thus, those sentient beings are enabled to see the color of the Tathāgata—the King of Wish-Fulfilling Jewels named ‘The Sound of the Ocean of Non-differentiated Wisdom that Causes Entry into the Inconceivable’—without any obstruction.”
Why is this? Because they have attained correspondence with the unique qualities (*āveṇika-dharma*). "Mañjuśrī!..."
It is like a great king of wish-fulfilling jewels made of lapis lazuli that is wrapped in a soiled garment; because of this soiled garment, various things appear.

Yet, the great king of wish-fulfilling jewels made of lapis lazuli does not discriminate and is free from discrimination, being naturally thus; without discrimination and free from discrimination, it is naturally thus, yet various things appear.
Why is this? Because it is associated with the unique qualities (āveṇika-dharma). "Mañjuśrī!
In this way, the Buddhas, Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, relying upon sentient beings who are capable of being transformed, manifest various forms and conducts.

Yet these Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, do not discriminate and are free from discrimination; they are naturally thus, without discrimination and free from discrimination, naturally thus, such that various and diverse matters are visible.
Why is this? Because they have attained correspondence with the unique qualities (āveṇika-dharma). “Mañjuśrī!
This is called the unimpeded wisdom of all Buddhas, Tathāgatas. "Mañjuśrī,
what is the unimpeded wisdom of all Buddhas, Tathāgatas?"

“Mañjuśrī! As for what are called the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, throughout the various and diverse worlds of the ten directions—in each and every world, as numerous as the atoms within those worlds—they cause them to enter the great ocean of wisdom regarding such atomically numerous worlds, without any obstruction.”

“Mañjuśrī! In all the various and diverse worlds, in each and every world, in each and every set of four continents, there are oceans of adornments consisting of as many diverse merits as there are atoms in all worlds. Within every moment of thought, there is unimpeded wisdom that articulates an incalculable number (*asaṃkhyeya*) of diverse teachings regarding these merits.”

"In this way, regarding all such various and distinct worlds, there is an ocean of wisdom adorned with merits, as numerous as the atoms within all Buddha-lands; in every moment of thought, there is unimpeded wisdom that expresses these in incalculable and diverse ways."

“In this way, within every thought-moment, there are incalculable and diverse modes of knowledge for expounding the great oceans of *pāramitās*, as numerous as the atoms in all Buddha-lands throughout these various and distinct worlds, without any obstruction.”

"In this way, within every moment of thought, there are incalculable and diverse modes of knowledge for expounding the teachings regarding the great oceans of dwelling stages, as numerous as the atoms in all the Buddha-lands throughout these various and distinct worlds, without any obstruction."

"In this way, within every thought-moment, there are incalculable and diverse knowledges of exposition regarding the great oceans of dhāraṇīs, as numerous as the atoms in all Buddha-lands throughout these various and distinct worlds, without any obstruction."

"In this way, within each and every thought-moment, there are incalculable and diverse modes of wisdom for expounding the great oceans of samādhis—equal in number to the atoms of all Buddha-lands throughout these various and distinct worlds—without any obstruction."

"In this way, within every thought-moment, there are incalculable and diverse knowledges of teaching regarding the great oceans of liberation, as numerous as the atoms in all Buddha-lands throughout these various and distinct worlds, without any obstruction."

"In this way, within every thought-moment, there are incalculable and diverse knowledges of speech regarding the great ocean of unhindered eloquence, as numerous as the atoms in all Buddha-lands throughout these various and distinct worlds, all of which are free from obstruction."

"In this way, within each moment of thought, there are incalculable and diverse knowledges of speech regarding the great oceans of spiritual powers, as numerous as the atoms in all Buddha-lands throughout these various and distinct worlds, without any obstruction."

"In this way, regarding the great ocean of vows as numerous as the atoms in all Buddha-lands throughout these various and diverse worlds, there is, in every moment of thought, an incalculable variety of unhindered wisdom for explaining them."

"In this way, throughout all these various and diverse worlds, within oceans of great diligence as numerous as the atoms of all Buddha-lands, there arise in every moment incalculable and diverse modes of wisdom for teaching, free from all obstruction."

"In this way, within the great ocean of peace and security, which is as numerous as the atoms of all Buddha-lands throughout these various and diverse worlds, there arise in every moment of thought incalculable and diverse modes of wisdom, free from all obstruction."

“In this way, throughout various and diverse worlds, as numerous as the atoms within all Buddha-lands, they cause them to enter the great ocean of Bodhisattva practices; in every moment of thought, they possess incalculable and diverse wisdoms of exposition, free from all obstruction.”

"In this way, he causes all the various and diverse worlds—the number of atoms in all Buddha-lands—to enter the great ocean of the Tathāgata; in every moment of thought, there is unimpeded, incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) wisdom of diverse teachings."

"In this way, within all the various and diverse worlds—equal in number to the atoms of all Buddha-lands—he causes them to enter the great ocean of the mental activities of sentient beings in accordance with their inclinations; in every moment of thought, he possesses incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) and diverse wisdoms of exposition, free from all obstruction."

"In this way, within an ocean of kalpas as numerous as the atoms in all Buddha-lands across these various and diverse worlds, there is, in every moment of thought, an incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) variety of wisdom for explaining [the Dharma] in different ways, free from all obstruction."

"In this way, within every thought-moment, there are incalculable and diverse modes of knowledge for entering the great ocean of worlds—worlds as numerous as the atoms in all Buddha-lands—without any obstruction."

"In this way, within the great ocean of teachings spoken throughout the three periods of time, causing all atoms within the Buddha-lands of these various and diverse worlds to enter therein, there exists in every moment of thought an incalculable variety of unhindered wisdom of speech."

"In this way, they cause all the various and diverse worlds—equal in number to the atoms of all Buddha-lands—to enter the great ocean of the three periods of time; in every moment of thought, they possess incalculable, diverse wisdoms of exposition, free from all obstruction."

"In this way, they cause all the various and diverse worlds—equal in number to the atoms of all Buddha-lands—to enter into the great ocean of a tireless mind; in every thought-moment, they possess incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) and diverse wisdoms of exposition, free from all obstruction."

"In this way, they cause all the various and distinct worlds—equal in number to the atoms of all Buddha-lands—to enter the great ocean of non-discriminative wisdom; within every moment of thought, they possess incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) and diverse modes of wisdom for teaching, free from all obstruction."
Why is this? Because they have attained spontaneous wisdom (*svayambhū-jñāna*). "Mañjuśrī!..."

For example, when an echo is heard within mountains, rivers, deep valleys, and the like, various distinct echoes emerge corresponding to various distinct sounds and various distinct names; yet the mountains, valleys, and so forth do not discriminate or engage in discrimination, but rather, being naturally thus without volition, without discrimination, and free from discrimination, they naturally manifest these various sounds in this way.
Why is this? Because it is associated with the unique qualities (āveṇika-dharma). "Mañjuśrī!

The vocal sounds of the Dharma preached by all Buddhas and Tathāgatas are likewise so: according to the minds of sentient beings and according to those among sentient beings who are capable of being transformed, various Dharma gates, various sounds, and various self-explanations are heard; yet the Buddhas and Tathāgatas do not discriminate nor are they apart from discrimination. Being naturally thus, without discrimination and apart from discrimination, they are naturally thus as these various sounds manifest.
Why is this? Because they have attained correspondence with the unique qualities (*āveṇika-dharma*). "Mañjuśrī!..."

This is called a brief explanation of the unobstructed wisdom of all Buddhas and Tathāgatas; if explained in detail, it could not be fully expressed even if one were to remain for as many eons as there are until the end of the future.
“Mañjuśrī! What is the power of the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, to teach and transform sentient beings? Mañjuśrī!”

What is called the *uṣṇīṣa* of all Buddhas and Tathāgatas pervades all worlds throughout the ten directions, in every dwelling place, in each and every world, and in each and every Jambudvīpa; it is without obstruction or hindrance, without distinction, and completely covers the entire space of the Dharma-realm. It teaches and transforms sentient beings in all worlds until the end of the future, reaching throughout boundless realms, remaining and sustaining them for kalpas without ever ceasing.

“Mañjuśrī! Thus, regarding each of the thirty-two marks of a Tathāgata, throughout the worlds of the ten directions, in all worlds, in every dwelling place, in each and every world, and in each Jambudvīpa, they are unobstructed and unhindered, without distinction, pervading the entirety of space and the Dharma-realm. They teach and transform sentient beings in all worlds until the end of the future, reaching everywhere across boundless worlds, remaining and sustaining themselves through kalpas without ever ceasing.”

“Mañjuśrī! Thus, regarding each of the Tathāgata’s eighty minor marks, throughout the worlds of the ten directions, in all worlds, in every dwelling place, in each and every world, and in each Jambudvīpa, they are unobstructed and unhindered, without distinction, pervading the entirety of the space of the Dharma-realm. They teach and transform sentient beings in all worlds until the end of the future, reaching everywhere across boundless worlds, remaining and sustaining them through kalpas without rest.”

“Mañjuśrī! Thus, from every single pore of the Tathāgata’s body, throughout all worlds in the ten directions, in every dwelling place of every world, and in every Jambudvīpa of every world—unobstructed, unimpeded, and without distinction—they pervade the entirety of space and the Dharma-realm. They teach and transform sentient beings in all worlds until the end of the future, reaching everywhere across boundless worlds and eons, remaining and sustaining them without rest.”

“Mañjuśrī! In this way, all the life-sustaining requisites of the Tathāgata—in the worlds of the ten directions, in all worlds, in all dwelling places, in each and every world, and in each and every Jambudvīpa—are without obstruction or hindrance, without distinction, and pervade the entirety of space and the Dharma-realm. They teach and transform sentient beings throughout all worlds until the end of the future, remaining and sustaining themselves throughout the kalpas of boundless worlds without ever ceasing.”
Why is this? Because it is associated with the uncommon dharmas (*āveṇikadharma*).

Being associated with the uncommon dharmas means, on the one hand, by virtue of the power of original vows, and on the other hand, by virtue of the sustaining power for the sake of all sentient beings.

“Mañjuśrī! This is called a brief explanation of the power of the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, to teach and transform sentient beings; were it to be explained in detail, even if one were to remain for as many eons as there are until the end of the future, it could not be fully told.”
“Mañjuśrī! How do the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, manifest before all gates? Mañjuśrī!”

That which is called the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, throughout the worlds of the ten directions, in all worlds, in all dwelling places, in each and every world, in each and every Jambudvīpa, and in every single atom.

Mañjuśrī! Beyond oceans of world-dust particles equal in number to the dust motes of fifty worlds, and beyond as many as the dust motes of hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas of asaṃkhyeya worlds—within each of these worlds, there dwell oceans of bodhisattvas with various distinctions as numerous as the dust motes of those worlds—and yet he dwells therein without any obstruction.

All sentient beings dwelling upon the four continents, the various Sumeru mountains, Mahāsumeru, Cakravāḍa mountains, Mahācakravāḍa mountains, cities, towns, villages, and all such lands, as well as the great rivers and large lakes, experience no obstruction; everything remains exactly as it was before, yet this phenomenon occurs.

Why is this? Because they have attained the correspondence with the unique qualities (*āveṇika-dharma*), they manifest before all beings according to their minds and according to what each can be transformed by—whether devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, Śakra, Brahmā, humans, non-humans, or various bodhisattvas—so that each and every one sees the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, appearing universally before them.
Why is this? Because they have attained correspondence with the unique qualities (āveṇika-dharma). "Mañjuśrī!
For example, on the fifteenth day at midnight during the waxing moon, all men and women, boys and girls within Jambudvīpa, see the lunar disc appearing before them.
And that lunar disc, without discrimination and free from discrimination, is naturally thus; without discrimination and free from discrimination, it is naturally thus, such that all things are seen.
Why is this? Because it is associated with the unique qualities (āveṇika-dharma). "Mañjuśrī!

The Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, are likewise so: throughout the worlds of the ten directions and all worlds, for the sentient beings dwelling therein, according to the minds of those beings and according to their capacity for transformation, each and every one perceives the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, appearing before them.

Yet all Buddhas and Tathāgatas do not conceptualize and are free from conceptualization; they are spontaneously thus, without conceptualization and free from conceptualization, spontaneously thus, such that all things are seen.
Why is this? Because they have attained correspondence with the unique qualities (āveṇika-dharma). "Mañjuśrī!..."

This is called a brief explanation of the universal manifestation of all Buddhas and Tathāgatas; were it to be explained in detail, it could not be fully recounted even if one were to remain for as many eons as there are until the end of the future.
“Mañjuśrī! How do the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, purify their Buddha-fields? Mañjuśrī!”

Regarding the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas: throughout the worlds of the ten directions, in all worlds, in every variety of dwelling place, and within each and every world, even within every single atom, they enter the great ocean of merit-adornments that comprises oceans of worlds as numerous as the atoms of all worlds.

Therein, they possess an incalculable number of diverse explanatory wisdoms capable of purifying them; or there are great oceans of merit-adornment through the wisdom of world-oceans, wherein they possess an incalculable number of diverse explanatory wisdoms capable of purifying them;
or there are great oceans of pāramitās of world-oceans, wherein they possess an incalculable number of diverse explanatory wisdoms capable of purifying them.
There may be oceans of world-systems that are oceans of the ground of abiding, which can be purified by incalculable, diverse wisdoms of exposition;
there may be oceans of world-systems that are oceans of dhāraṇīs, which can be purified by incalculable, diverse wisdoms of exposition;
there may be oceans of world-systems that are oceans of samādhis, which can be purified by incalculable, diverse wisdoms of exposition.
There are oceans of world-systems that are oceans of liberation, which can be purified by incalculable, diverse knowledges of exposition;
there are oceans of world-systems that are oceans of unimpeded eloquence, which can be purified by incalculable, diverse knowledges of exposition;
and there are oceans of world-systems that are oceans of supernormal powers, which can be purified by incalculable, diverse knowledges of exposition.
There may be oceans of world-systems that are great oceans of vast vows, which can be purified by incalculable varieties of knowledge for explaining them;
there may be oceans of world-systems that are great oceans of the exertion of diligent vigor, which can be purified by incalculable varieties of knowledge for explaining them;
there may be oceans of world-systems that are great oceans of attaining peace and security, which can be purified by incalculable varieties of knowledge for explaining them.
There are world-oceans that cause one to enter the great ocean of bodhisattva practices, which are purified by incalculable, diverse modes of knowledge;
there are world-oceans that cause one to enter the great ocean of the Tathāgatas, which are purified by incalculable, diverse modes of knowledge;
and there are world-oceans that cause one to enter the great ocean of conforming to the mental activities of sentient beings, which are purified by incalculable, diverse modes of knowledge.
There are world-oceans that cause entry into the great ocean of eons, which can be purified by an incalculable variety of wisdoms of diverse explanations;
there are world-oceans that cause entry into the great ocean of worlds, which can be purified by an incalculable variety of wisdoms of diverse explanations;

and there are world-oceans that cause entry into the great ocean of explanations regarding the three periods of time, which can be purified by an incalculable variety of wisdoms of diverse explanations.
There are world-oceans that cause entry into the great ocean of the three periods of time, which are purified by incalculable, diverse knowledges of exposition;
there are world-oceans that cause entry into the great ocean of the tireless mind, which are purified by incalculable, diverse knowledges of exposition;
and there are world-oceans that cause entry into the great ocean of non-discriminative knowledge, which are purified by incalculable, diverse knowledges of exposition.
Yet the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, do not move from their original place. Why is this?
Because they have attained the dharma of immovability.

“Mañjuśrī! This is a brief explanation of how all the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, possess pure Buddha-lands and are free from fear; were it to be explained in detail, it could not be fully recounted even if one were to remain and maintain it throughout the kalpas until the end of the future.”
“Mañjuśrī! What is the boundless body of all Buddhas, the Tathāgatas? Mañjuśrī!”
That which is called the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, throughout the worlds of the ten directions— every single world,
every single set of four continents within those worlds— beyond oceans of world-microdust as numerous as the microdust of fifty worlds,
and beyond Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, as numerous as the microdust of hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas of asaṃkhyeya worlds.
The great assemblies of Bodhisattvas—each of these great oceans of Bodhisattva assemblies surpasses the number of atoms in fifty world-systems;

within each of these great oceans of Bodhisattva assemblies are as many Buddhas, Tathāgatas, and Bodhisattva assemblies as there are atoms in hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas of asaṃkhyeyas of worlds. Each of these great oceans of Bodhisattva assemblies...
Each and every one of them was adorned by a great ocean of various and diverse, countless,
and supreme merits; because they were sustained by the power of such various and diverse, supreme merits,
they all attained the direct vision of that same number of Buddha-Tathāgatas.

“Mañjuśrī! Beyond oceans of world-dust particles as numerous as the dust motes in fifty worlds, there are assemblies of Bodhisattvas before Buddhas, Tathāgatas, numbering as many as the dust motes in incalculable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas of worlds. Each of these oceans of Bodhisattva assemblies is individually adorned by an ocean of various and diverse supreme wisdom and merit-ornaments, each being incalculable. By virtue of the sustaining power of having attained such various and diverse adornments of supreme wisdom and merit, they are all able to see that same number of Buddhas, Tathāgatas, directly before their eyes.”

“Mañjuśrī! Beyond as many oceans of world-microdusts as there are microdusts in fifty worlds, there are as many great assemblies of Buddhas, Tathāgatas, and Bodhisattvas as there are microdusts in hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas of asaṃkhyeyas. Each of these great oceans of Bodhisattva assemblies is individually adorned by great oceans of various and diverse supreme pāramitās, each numbering as many asaṃkhyeyas. Because they are sustained by the power of having attained such various and diverse supreme pāramitās, all of them are able to see that same number of Buddhas, Tathāgatas, directly before their eyes.”

“Mañjuśrī! Beyond oceans of world-dust particles as numerous as the dust motes in fifty worlds, there are assemblies of Bodhisattvas before Buddhas, Tathāgatas, numbering as many as the dust motes in incalculable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas of worlds. Each of these oceans of Bodhisattva assemblies is individually adorned by oceans of various and diverse supreme stages of dwelling (bhūmi) that are themselves incalculable. Because they abide through the sustaining power of such various and diverse supreme stages of dwelling, all of them are able to see as many Buddhas, Tathāgatas as those [dust motes].”

“Mañjuśrī! Beyond oceans of world-dust particles as numerous as the dust motes of fifty worlds, there are hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas of oceans of world-dust particles of Buddhas, Tathāgatas, and assemblies of Bodhisattvas. Within each of these oceans of Bodhisattva assemblies, every single one is adorned by oceans of various and diverse supreme dhāraṇīs, numbering as many as the dust motes of asaṃkhyeyas. Because they are sustained by the power of such various and diverse supreme dhāraṇīs, they are all able to see before them that same number of Buddhas, Tathāgatas.”

“Mañjuśrī! Beyond oceans of world-dust particles as numerous as the dust motes of fifty worlds, there are Bodhisattvas of Buddhas, Tathāgatas, numbering as many as the dust motes of incalculable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas. Within each of these great oceans of assemblies of Bodhisattvas, every single assembly is individually adorned by great oceans of various and diverse, supreme samādhis, numbering as many as incalculable [particles]. Because they abide through the sustaining power of such various and diverse, supreme samādhis, they are all able to directly behold that same number of Buddhas, Tathāgatas.”

“Mañjuśrī! Beyond as many oceans of world-microdusts as there are microdusts in fifty worlds, there are as many great assemblies of Buddha-Tathāgatas and Bodhisattvas as there are microdusts in hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas of asaṃkhyeyas. Each of these great oceans of Bodhisattva assemblies is individually adorned by an ocean of various and diverse supreme liberations, each numbering asaṃkhyeyas. Because they abide in and are sustained by the power of such various and diverse supreme liberations, they are all able to directly perceive that same number of Buddha-Tathāgatas.”

"Mañjuśrī! Beyond oceans of world-dust particles as numerous as the dust motes in fifty world-systems, there are hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas of oceans of dust-motes of Buddhas, Tathāgatas, and assemblies of Bodhisattvas. Within each of these oceans of assemblies of Bodhisattvas, every single assembly is individually adorned by an ocean of various, diverse, supreme, and unimpeded eloquence that is itself incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*). Because they are sustained by the power of having attained such various, diverse, supreme, and unimpeded eloquence, they are all able to directly perceive as many Buddhas, Tathāgatas as there are those very dust-motes."

“Mañjuśrī! Beyond oceans of world-dust particles as numerous as the dust motes in fifty world-systems, there are oceans of assemblies of Bodhisattvas belonging to hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas of *asaṃkhyeya* Buddhas and Tathāgatas. Each of these oceans of Bodhisattva assemblies is individually adorned by an ocean of various and diverse, supreme supernormal powers (*abhijñā*) that are themselves *asaṃkhyeya*. Because they abide through the sustaining power of such various and diverse, supreme supernormal faculties, they are all able to see directly as many Buddhas and Tathāgatas as those [dust motes].”

“Mañjuśrī! Beyond oceans of world-microdusts, as numerous as the microdusts of fifty world-systems, there are assemblies of Buddhas, Tathāgatas, and Bodhisattvas numbering as many as the microdusts of incalculable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas. Each of these oceans of Bodhisattva assemblies is individually adorned by an ocean of various and diverse supreme great vows, each numbering as many as incalculable [vows]. Because they abide through the sustaining power of such various and diverse supreme great vows, all of them are able to directly behold that same number of Buddhas, Tathāgatas.”

“Mañjuśrī! Beyond oceans of world-dust atoms equal in number to the dust atoms of fifty worlds, there are as many great assemblies of Buddha-Tathāgatas and Bodhisattvas as there are dust atoms in hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas of asaṃkhyeyas. Within each of these oceans of great Bodhisattva assemblies, every single assembly is individually adorned by an ocean of various and diverse, supreme, and diligent efforts, all of which are asaṃkhyeya in number. Because they abide in and are sustained by such powers of various and diverse, supreme, and diligent efforts, they are all able to directly behold that same number of Buddha-Tathāgatas.”

“Mañjuśrī! Beyond oceans of world-dust particles as numerous as the dust motes of fifty worlds, there are hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas of oceans of world-dust particles of Buddhas, Tathāgatas, and assemblies of Bodhisattvas. Each of these oceans of assemblies of Bodhisattvas is individually adorned by oceans of various and diverse supreme attainments of peace, each numbering as many as asaṃkhyeyas. Because they abide through the sustaining power of having attained such various and diverse supreme attainments of peace, they are all able to see as many Buddhas, Tathāgatas as that number manifest before them.”

“Mañjuśrī! Beyond oceans of world-microdusts, as numerous as the microdusts of fifty worlds, there are assemblies of Buddhas, Tathāgatas, and Bodhisattvas numbering as many as the microdusts of incalculable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas. Within each of these oceans of Bodhisattva assemblies, every single assembly has attained an ocean of various and distinct, supreme means for entering the Bodhisattva practices, which they use to adorn themselves. Because they abide in and are sustained by such powers of various and distinct, supreme means for entering the Bodhisattva practices, they are all able to see that same number of Buddhas, Tathāgatas, manifest before their eyes.”

“Mañjuśrī! Beyond oceans of world-dust particles as numerous as the dust motes in fifty worlds, there are assemblies of Bodhisattvas before Buddhas, Tathāgatas, numbering as many as the dust motes in incalculable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas of worlds. Each of these oceans of Bodhisattva assemblies has attained incalculable varieties of diverse and supreme qualities that cause them to enter the ocean of the Tathāgatas, thereby adorning themselves. Because they have attained such various and diverse supreme qualities that cause them to abide in the sustaining power of the Tathāgata, they are all able to see as many Buddhas, Tathāgatas, as those very numbers.”

“Mañjuśrī! Beyond oceans of world-microdusts, as numerous as the microdusts of fifty worlds, there are assemblies of Bodhisattvas before Buddhas, Tathāgatas, numbering as many as the microdusts of incalculable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas. Each of these oceans of Bodhisattva assemblies has attained an incalculable variety of diverse and supreme powers for entering and acceding to the mental activities of sentient beings, thereby adorning themselves. Because they abide in the sustaining power of such diverse and supreme abilities for entering and acceding to the mental activities of sentient beings, they are all able to see that same number of Buddhas, Tathāgatas, manifest before them.”

“Mañjuśrī! Beyond oceans of world-microdusts, as numerous as the microdusts of fifty world-systems, there are assemblies of Bodhisattvas before Buddhas, Tathāgatas, numbering as many as the microdusts of incalculable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas. Each of these oceans of Bodhisattva assemblies has individually attained oceans of various and diverse supreme methods for entering eons, with which they adorn themselves. Because they abide in the sustaining power of having attained such various and diverse supreme methods for entering eons, they are all able to directly behold that same number of Buddhas, Tathāgatas.”

“Mañjuśrī! Beyond oceans of world-microdusts, as numerous as the microdusts of fifty world-systems, there are assemblies of Bodhisattvas before Buddhas, Tathāgatas, numbering as many as the microdusts of incalculable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas. Each of these oceans of Bodhisattva assemblies is individually adorned by an ocean of various and diverse supreme means for entering worlds, each numbering as many as incalculable varieties. Because they abide in the sustaining power of such various and diverse supreme means for entering worlds, they are all able to directly behold that same number of Buddhas, Tathāgatas.”

"Mañjuśrī! Beyond oceans of world-dust particles as numerous as the dust motes of fifty worlds, there are assemblies of Bodhisattvas before Buddhas, Tathāgatas, numbering as many as the dust motes of hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas of asaṃkhyeyas. Each of these oceans of Bodhisattva assemblies has individually attained various and diverse kinds of supreme powers for entering the ocean of teachings on the three periods of time to adorn themselves. Because they abide in and maintain such various and diverse kinds of supreme powers for entering the ocean of teachings on the three periods of time, they are all able to directly perceive that same number of Buddhas, Tathāgatas."

“Mañjuśrī! Beyond oceans of world-microdusts as numerous as the microdusts of fifty worlds, there are assemblies of Bodhisattvas before Buddhas, Tathāgatas, numbering as many as the microdusts of hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas of asaṃkhyeyas. Each of these oceans of Bodhisattva assemblies has individually attained various and diverse kinds of supreme dharmas for entering the great ocean of the three periods of time to adorn themselves. Because they abide in and are sustained by such various and diverse kinds of supreme powers for entering the three periods of time, they are all able to see that same number of Buddhas, Tathāgatas directly before their eyes.”

“Mañjuśrī! Beyond oceans of world-dust particles as numerous as the dust motes in fifty worlds, there are assemblies of Bodhisattvas before Buddhas, Tathāgatas, numbering as many as the dust motes in hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas of asaṃkhyeyas. Each of these oceans of Bodhisattva assemblies has individually attained an ocean of various and diverse, supreme, tireless minds that lead others into [the Dharma], thereby adorning themselves. Because they abide in and are sustained by such powers of various and diverse, supreme, tireless minds that lead others into [the Dharma], they are all able to directly behold as many Buddhas, Tathāgatas as those numbers.”

“Mañjuśrī! Beyond oceans of world-dust particles as numerous as the dust motes of fifty world-systems, there are as many great assemblies of Buddha-Tathāgatas and Bodhisattvas as there are dust motes in hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas of asaṃkhyeyas. Within each of these oceans of Bodhisattva assemblies, every single one has attained an ocean of various and diverse, supreme, non-differentiating wisdoms that lead others into entry, thereby adorning themselves. Because they abide in and are sustained by such powers of various and diverse, supreme, non-differentiating wisdoms that lead others into entry, they are all able to see face-to-face as many Buddha-Tathāgatas as those very numbers.”
“Mañjuśrī! Thus, in brief, have been explained the attainment of various supports, various marvelous signs, practices, spiritual friends,
the exertion of diligent effort, the attainment of mental tranquility, the teaching and transforming of sentient beings, the precepts, and the receiving of predictions.”
Entering the conduct of bodhisattvas, entering the conduct of Tathāgatas, entering the conduct of sentient beings, entering the oceans of worlds, entering the oceans of eons,
entering the dharmas of the three periods of time; entering the arousal of the mind without weariness, the various distinctions of wisdom,
the gates of dhāraṇī, the teachings of all Tathāgatas, and the various minds of Samantabhadra.
The universal conduct of Samantabhadra, the great compassionate mind of various dharmic characteristics, the causes and conditions of the bodhisattva mind,
reverence for spiritual friends, the practices of generating the resolve, the purification of all cultivations, the various pāramitās, awakening to reality as it is,
attaining entry into reality as it is, the powers and sublime powers, and all forms of equanimity.
The Way consists in expounding all Buddha-dharmas, specializing in eloquence, the predominance of various wisdoms,
attaining non-attachment, achieving equanimity of mind, initiating various forms of knowledge, performing various transformations, upholding all dharmas,
attaining great peace and stability, entering all profound dharmas, and dwelling in reliance upon the Buddha and reliance upon the Dharma.
He attains a mind of loving-kindness and a mind free from cowardice; he severs all webs of doubt; he gives rise to the mind of aspiration and the inconceivable mind;
he understands by what intention various skillful means are taught and how they are explained through the distinctions of various wisdoms;
he attains all samādhis, all spheres of totality (*kṛtsnāyatana*), all liberations, and all supernormal powers (*abhijñā*).
All vidyās; the liberation of attaining mastery over all minds; all exquisite ponds; all sublime pavilions;
all supreme adornments; all non-retrogressive minds; abiding in the mind of non-abandonment;
all straightforward minds; entry into wisdom like the ocean; being like various jewels; and the bodhisattva’s resolve for enlightenment being like a diamond.
...and gives rise to the resolve for awakening, the Mahāyāna resolve, the impartial resolve, and the ultimate resolve;
attains an indestructible mind of reverence; receives the prophecy of enlightenment; dedicates all dharmas and all roots of goodness; attains wisdom;
increases the supreme, boundless, and centerless impartial resolve for awakening; and obtains all treasuries of jewels.
Having attained all the prohibitions and precepts, all masteries, all heroic strides, all spheres of activity, all powers, and all fearlessnesses;
being fully endowed with immeasurable unshared dharmas to teach and transform all bodhisattvas;
and having attained all karmas of body and all bodies, as well as all karmas of speech.
...all minds, the arousal of the mind, the pervasiveness of the mind, universally covering all faculties,
all upright minds, all superior minds, all practices, all faiths, entering the world of faith,
entering various habitual tendencies, attaining entry into all grasping, entering into practice according to reality, entering into accomplished practice, entering into bodhi...
The stage of the bodhisattva; the fixed nature of all bodhisattva dharmas; the path of progress toward all dharmas; drawing near to spiritual friends; attaining spiritual friends;
what is the path and what is not the path; what is valid cognition and what is not valid cognition;
accomplishing the vision of the path; possessing the merits of the path; practicing the cognition of the path; and the adornments of all paths.

“Mañjuśrī! In this way, each and every one of these should be explained in detail; yet the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, do not conceptualize nor are they free from conceptualization, but are naturally thus, without conceptualization and free from conceptualization, naturally thus manifesting in various ways.”
Why is this? Because they have attained correspondence with the unique qualities (āveṇika-dharma). "Mañjuśrī!..."

In this way, the Tathāgata simultaneously manifests throughout all worlds and all dwelling places in the worlds of the ten directions; in each and every world, in each and every Jambudvīpa, he appears according to the capacity of those beings to be transformed, such that they perceive the various Buddhas and Tathāgatas. Yet these Buddhas and Tathāgatas do not engage in discrimination or depart from discrimination; they are naturally thus, without discrimination or departure from discrimination, naturally thus, manifesting in manifold ways.
Why is this? Because they have attained the correspondence with the unique qualities (āveṇika-dharma), and because they possess the unobstructed body of a Tathāgata. "Mañjuśrī!..."

This is called a brief explanation of the boundless bodies of all Buddhas and Tathāgatas; were it to be explained in detail, they could not be fully described even if one were to abide and maintain them throughout the kalpas of the future limit.
“Mañjuśrī! How do the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, see universally? Mañjuśrī!”
I shall speak by way of analogy. Why?
Because those possessed of wisdom can understand the meaning by relying upon various analogies.

Mañjuśrī! Suppose there were a great pool of water five hundred yojanas or a thousand yojanas in extent, overflowing and level with the ground, its surface entirely covered by the petals of a great lotus flower. Upon these lotus petals, there is a person riding an iron chariot; this iron chariot possesses a thousand spokes, and the horses yoked to it travel with such speed that they surpass even the garuḍa bird.
As that iron chariot travels with such speed, the water does not wet the wheels, the spokes, or the horses' hooves; neither the wheels nor the horses' hooves damage the petals of the flowers.
As that man on the lake traveled in such a carriage, at that very moment, a great venomous serpent arose within the pool.
At what time did those carriage wheels and the horse's hooves turn but once?
At the moment he thought of it, that great venomous snake coiled around the chariot seven times. "Mañjuśrī!
At what time did that great venomous snake coil around the chariot once?"
Based on that moment, the bhikṣu Ānanda preached the Dharma ten times, and furthermore, he further manifested its meaning.
At what time did the bhikṣu Ānanda preach the Dharma once?
Based on that single moment, the bhikṣu Śāriputra preached the Dharma a thousand times to make sentient beings understand.
At what time did the bhikṣu Śāriputra preach the Dharma only once?
In that single moment, Mahāmaudgalyāyana can pass beyond eighty thousand worlds.
In what duration of time does Mahāmaudgalyāyana pass through a single world?

Based on that single moment, all Buddhas and Tathāgatas—in every world and every dwelling place, in each and every world and each Jambudvīpa—at one and the same time, and not at successive times, descend from Tuṣita Heaven, renounce the world, practice austerities, sit at the site of enlightenment, subdue the hosts of Māra, manifest the realization of perfect awakening, turn the wheel of Dharma, demonstrate Great Nirvāṇa, maintain the Buddha-dharma, and show the extinction of all phenomena; they are able to cause all these deeds, including their various birthplaces among the ranks of non-Buddhist practitioners, to be seen simultaneously, rather than being seen sequentially.
Why is this? Because it is without obstruction.
That which is without obstruction is without differentiation; that which is without differentiation is without dependence.
“Mañjuśrī! It is like a great lapis lazuli wish-fulfilling jewel wrapped in a priceless colored cloth; because of that cloth, various forms are perceived.”

Yet the great lapis lazuli wish-fulfilling jewel, without discrimination and free from discrimination, is naturally thus; without discrimination and free from discrimination, it is naturally thus, manifesting various appearances.
Why is this? Because they have attained correspondence with the unique qualities (āveṇika-dharma). "Mañjuśrī!..."

The Buddhas, Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, are likewise thus: depending upon sentient beings who are capable of being transformed, throughout the worlds of the ten directions, in all worlds, and in all dwelling places, at one and the same time—not at successive times—they appear in such various different ways in every single thought-moment.

Yet the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, are neither conceptualizing nor free from conceptualization; they are spontaneously thus. Being without conceptualization and free from conceptualization, they are spontaneously thus, yet appear through various different perceptions.
Why is this? Because they have attained correspondence with the unique qualities (āveṇika-dharma). "Mañjuśrī!..."

For example, it is like the lunar disk or the solar disk, which appear clearly in all the waters of the vessels throughout Jambudvīpa—provided they are pure and unturbid and free from obstructions—yet the disks of the sun and moon do not move from their original positions.

“Mañjuśrī! Thus, for the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, throughout the worlds of the ten directions and all worlds, there is no obstruction and no hindrance; in such and such ways, according to those beings who can be transformed and whose own minds are purified, they all see the Tathāgata.”

Yet the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, remain as they were, unmoved from Tuṣita Heaven; nevertheless, they appear before all sentient beings throughout all worlds in the ten directions, manifesting within the minds that give rise to them.
Why is this? Because the Tathāgata has attained non-retrogressive wisdom. "Mañjuśrī!

For example, just as all sentient beings in the world, by virtue of their inferior, middling, or superior karmic retributions, fully accomplish inferior, middling, or superior conditioned formations (*saṃskāra*), yet these conditioned formations are without discrimination and free from discrimination, being spontaneously so; and being without discrimination and free from discrimination, they are spontaneously so—thus various such matters are accomplished.
Why is this? Because they have attained correspondence with the unique qualities (āveṇika-dharma). “Mañjuśrī!
Thus, depending on the retribution of their inferior, middling, or superior karma, these sentient beings perceive the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, as being inferior, middling, or superior.

Yet the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, do not discriminate and are free from discrimination; they are naturally thus, without discrimination and free from discrimination, naturally thus appearing as inferior, middling, or superior.
Why is this? Because they have attained correspondence with the unique qualities (āveṇika-dharma). “Mañjuśrī!
For example, when a single rain with a single color, taste, and so forth falls upon Jambudvīpa, depending on various vessels, it takes on various colors, various tastes, and various fragrances.

Yet the great rain falls without discrimination or the absence of discrimination; it is naturally thus, without discrimination or the absence of discrimination, being naturally so. The colors, fragrances, and tastes are distinct.
Why is this? Because they have attained correspondence with the unique qualities (*āveṇika-dharma*). "Mañjuśrī!..."
In this way, although all Buddhas, Tathāgatas, abide in the single-flavored Dharma-realm, they perceive various differentiated phenomena according to the beings who are to be transformed.

Yet, these Buddhas, Tathāgatas do not engage in discrimination and are free from discrimination; they are naturally so—without discrimination, free from discrimination, and naturally so—they perceive differentiated phenomena. Why is this?
Because they are associated with the attainment of the unique qualities (*āveṇika-dharma*). "Mañjuśrī!
For example, wherever the sovereign wish-fulfilling jewel king (*cintāmaṇi-rāja*) is produced, in that place iron does not arise; various iron vessels do not grow there."
Why is this? Because they have attained correspondence with the unique qualities (āveṇika-dharma). "Mañjuśrī!

In this way, wherever the light of the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, arises, there the light of fire does not arise, nor the light of lightning, nor the light of the sun and moon; the light of various sovereign wish-fulfilling maṇi jewels does not arise, nor do the lights of devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, Śakra the Lord of Devas, Mahābrahmā, or the Four World-Protecting Kings.

In that place, the decrees of celestial kings do not prevail; there, the four castes are not born, and there, the eight kinds of difficult conditions—namely the hells, hungry ghosts, animals, and other such calamities—are not produced.

In that place, the ten paths of unwholesome action do not arise; in that place, various forms of disturbance do not arise; and in that place, other non-Buddhist sectarians, those who live by wrong livelihood, such as the Nirgranthas, and so forth, do not arise.

“Mañjuśrī! All Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, do not engage in conceptualization and are free from conceptualization; they are naturally thus, without conceptualization and free from conceptualization, naturally thus, such that no phenomena arise.”
Why is this? Because they have attained correspondence with the unique qualities (āveṇika-dharma). “Mañjuśrī!

This is called a brief explanation of the inconceivable realm of all Buddhas and Tathāgatas; were it to be explained in detail, it could not be fully recounted even if one were to remain for as many eons as exist until the end of the future.
